title: Medicare Advantage vs Original Medicare: The Plain Truth
bigPicture: Original Medicare is a federal fee-for-service plan; Medicare Advantage is a private plan that bundles your coverage — both meet the legal minimum, but they work very differently.
whatYouNeedToKnow: Original Medicare (Part A + Part B) lets you see any doctor nationwide that accepts Medicare — no referrals needed.
Medicare Advantage (Part C) is sold by private companies, often includes drug coverage and extras like dental or vision, but you must use its network.
Both cover hospital and doctor visits, but copays, premiums, and out-of-pocket limits differ — compare the yearly summary before you pick.
commonMistakesToAvoid: Assuming your current doctors are in-network — always check the plan's provider list first.
Skipping the yearly Open Enrollment review — your needs and costs change, so should your plan.
Thinking 'free' means no cost — look for premiums, deductibles, and copays.
actionSteps: Visit Medicare.gov or call 1-800-MEDICARE to compare plans in your zip code.
List your doctors, medications, and preferred hospitals, then match them to plan networks.
Set a calendar reminder for Open Enrollment (Oct 15 – Dec 7) to review and switch if needed.
